######## section -1
== rendered

   Nodes

  Every syntax that gives a selectable node, and syntax that looks like one
  but does not.

  ## Inline links

  A plain link 🔗 https://example.com/plain and one with a title 🔗
  https://example.com/title and an angle destination 🔗 https://example.com/with
  space.

  A URL with parentheses 🔗
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)#Unnamed and a space
  before it 🔗 https://example.com/space.

  A link whose text goes on 🔗 https://example.com/two-lines and one whose
  destination does: here 🔗 https://example.com/next-line.

  Nested brackets: [Become a backer 🔗 https://example.com/backer].

  A link with  code  🔗 https://example.com/code and bold 🔗
  https://example.com/bold.

  An anchor to a heading.

  ## Reference links

  The full 🔗 https://example.com/ref, the collapsed 🔗
  https://example.com/collapsed and the shortcut 🔗 https://example.com/shortcut
  forms, and an image badge 📷 https://example.com/badge.svg.

  ## Autolinks and bare URLs

  An autolink https://example.com/auto, a bare https://example.com/bare.
  Ending a sentence: https://example.com/end, or (https://example.com/paren).
  Mail someone@example.com and bare someone@example.com.

  Side by side: one 🔗 https://example.com/1 two 🔗 https://example.com/2, same 🔗
  https://example.com/1 url 🔗 https://example.com/1, anchor then 🔗
  https://example.com/3, and a link 🔗 https://example.com/4
  https://example.com/5.

  ## Images

  An inline image 📷 /img/a.png and a linked one: badge 📷
  https://example.com/b.svg 🔗 https://example.com/target.

  ## HTML

  Inline anchor tag 🔗 https://example.com/a-tag and image tag 📷 /img/tag.png in
  a paragraph.
  [![Logo](img/logo.png)](https://example.com/block-a)
    Text with `code` and [markdown](https://example.com/md) in an HTML block.
  ## Code spans

  A  span , a  span with ` inside , and  `  a backtick alone.

  A span that  goes on the next line  here.

   Operator                             │ Meaning
  ──────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────
    a | b                               │ either
    [x](y)                              │ no link

  Not a link inside code:  https://example.com/in-code  and  [t](u) .

  ### Heading with  code

  ## Code blocks

    fmt.Println("fenced")

    tilde fence

    trailing blank line follows


  • A list item:
    echo in-list


  │ Quoted:
  │
  │   in quote

    indented code
    and its second line


  Unclosed at the end:

    never closed

== rendered

   Nodes

  Every syntax that gives a selectable node, and syntax that looks like one
  but does not.

  ## Inline links

  A plain link 🔗 https://example.com/plain and one with a title 🔗
  https://example.com/title and an angle destination 🔗 https://example.com/with
  space.

  A URL with parentheses 🔗
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_number_(programming)#Unnamed and a space
  before it 🔗 https://example.com/space.

  A link whose text goes on 🔗 https://example.com/two-lines and one whose
  destination does: here 🔗 https://example.com/next-line.

  Nested brackets: [Become a backer 🔗 https://example.com/backer].

  A link with  code  🔗 https://example.com/code and bold 🔗
  https://example.com/bold.

  An anchor to a heading.

  ## Reference links

  The full 🔗 https://example.com/ref, the collapsed 🔗
  https://example.com/collapsed and the shortcut 🔗 https://example.com/shortcut
